text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Muhammad Muhammad Taib, who formally resigned as Selangor chief minister today, said he would hold on to his post as UMNO vice president until the 1999 party elections.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said tonight Malaysia would encourage the private sector to explore trade, economic and investment opportunities in Egypt.
-- The Control of Rent Act 1966 will be abolished on Sept 1 but the increase in rentals by building owners will be controlled during a three-year transition period.

-- In the biggest ever teleconferencing link-up in the country, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad will reach out to an expected audience of 13,000 to promote the Multimedia Super Corridor today. The teleconference will include state officials, teachers, students and government officials.

-- Profit guarantees by merchant banks for companies seeking a listing on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange are exempted from the recently announced Bank Negara lending guidelines while the initial public offerings of manufacturing and infrastructure companies will be considered on a case-by-case basis.
-- The Labuan International Offshore Financial Centre will be the underwriting centre for the next Tenaga Nasional Bhd bond offering, the first time a local company is using Labuan for the purpose.
